# Interactive Bayesian Inference Explorer

An interactive Shiny web application for exploring fundamental concepts in Bayesian statistics. This app is designed to build intuition for how prior beliefs combine with observed data to form a posterior distribution.

I am developing this project as part of the 'Introduction to Bayesian Modelling' module for my MSc in Health Data Science. It serves as a practical portfolio piece to demonstrate my growing skills in R, Shiny, and applied Bayesian methods on my journey to becoming a health data scientist.


## 🎯 Features

The app is organised as a learning path, with five pages in the top bar:

1. **Home:** a live "Bayes in ten seconds" demo, the prior × likelihood ∝ posterior idea, the learning path, and example questions from health and education that jump straight to the right tool.
2. **Bayesian Basics:** starts with **What is Bayes?**, a teaching tab on what Bayesian statistics is and why it helps (a worked example compared with a p-value, an interactive screening-test demo of Bayes' rule, a "priors wash out" animation, a frequentist vs Bayesian table and a glossary). Then come the Binomial, Poisson and Normal models with conjugate priors, introduced on a "Three models" tab.
3. **MCMC Simulations:** sampling-based inference with trace plots, densities and diagnostics.
4. **Prior Lab:** seven tools to explore and check priors (described below).
5. **Model Lab:** fit 11 data models with your own priors and data, and export Stan code.

This application allows you to interactively explore several common Bayesian models.

### Current Features

  * **Binomial Model (Discrete Prior):**
      * Interactively set the number of trials ($n$) and successes ($x$) from observed binomial data.
      * Define a **discrete prior distribution** by specifying possible values for the proportion ($\theta$) and their associated probabilities.
      * Instantly view the resulting Prior, Likelihood, and Posterior distributions in a clear table.
      * Visualize the prior and posterior distributions to see the "Bayesian update" in action, powered by the `TeachBayes` package.



  * **Binomial Model (Conjugate Prior):**

      * Implement the **Beta-Binomial** model.
      * Allow users to set prior beliefs using the Beta($\alpha$, $\beta$) distribution's parameters.
      * Visualize the continuous prior, likelihood, and posterior distributions on a single plot.
      (Left with point estimates and simulations)

### Prior Lab (advanced prior experimentation)

A menu of five tabs for choosing, checking and defending priors in real analyses:

  * **Prior Builder:** compare up to four priors from 14 families (Normal, Student-t, Cauchy, Logistic, Laplace, Uniform, Half-Normal, Half-t, Half-Cauchy, Exponential, Gamma, Inverse-Gamma, Log-Normal, Beta). See each prior on its own scale and on the **implied scale** after a link function (probability, odds/rate ratio, variance, precision), with tail probabilities and how much mass sits on extreme values. Export brms, Stan and R code, or download prior draws.
  * **Elicitation:** turn expert judgement into a prior. Enter 2-5 quantiles (SHELF-style least squares on the CDF) or a mean and SD, fit several families at once, compare the fits, and read back the fitted prior's quantiles as feedback.
  * **Prior → Posterior & Sensitivity:** any prior (or a robust two-component mixture) with a Binomial, Poisson or Normal likelihood, placed on the natural scale or the link scale (logit / log). The posterior is computed exactly on an adaptive grid. Includes:
      * equal-tailed or HDI intervals and a Jeffreys/flat reference posterior for comparison
      * power-scaling sensitivity of prior and likelihood (after Kallioinen et al., 2023) with a plain-language diagnosis
      * prior predictive check for prior-data conflict
      * approximate prior effective sample size
      * posterior weight on each mixture component
      * Stan and brms code for the same model
  * **Prior Predictive (regression):** simulate from intercept, slope and residual-SD priors for linear, logistic and Poisson regression with up to 20 standardised predictors, and compare the implied outcomes with what is plausible. Shows how priors on many coefficients compound.
  * **Hierarchical priors:**
      * what a prior on the group-level SD τ implies about differences between groups (e.g. odds ratio between top and bottom 10% of modules)
      * exact partial pooling for the 8 schools model, or your own group estimates, with any prior on τ or τ², Gelman (2006) presets, shrinkage profiles and forest plots
      * marginal LKJ prior for correlations between random effects

  * **Advanced priors:**
      * shrinkage priors for many predictors (Normal, Laplace, regularised horseshoe, R2D2, spike-and-slab), showing the R² each implies
      * Dirichlet priors for shares that sum to 1 (with brms `mo()` and Stan code)
      * Inverse-Wishart vs LKJ + independent SDs for covariance matrices
  * **Presets:** 24 documented priors for health (sceptical/enthusiastic trial priors, meta-analysis heterogeneity, survival, diagnostic accuracy), education (effect sizes, between-module variation, Likert cutpoints, IRT) and general use, each with a rationale and reference. Quick builders turn plain statements into priors: "the SD is unlikely to exceed U", "about m, worth n observations", "I'm p sure the effect is within ±d".
  * **Model Lab:** pick one of 11 data models, use the example data (health and education stories) or upload a CSV, and set a prior for every parameter; the prior inputs update with the model.
      * Normal, Student-t, log-normal, Gamma, Bernoulli/logistic, Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson, Beta, ordinal (cumulative logit, for Likert items), Weibull survival with censoring; each with an optional predictor
      * live prior predictive checks, then posterior, posterior predictive checks, trace plots and R-hat / bulk and tail ESS (Vehtari et al., 2021)
      * an in-app sampler: 4 chains of adaptive Metropolis mixed with an independence proposal, started from the posterior mode; fits take 1-2 seconds
      * WAIC model comparison (e.g. Poisson vs negative binomial vs zero-inflated)
      * a complete **Stan program** (with `y_rep` and `log_lik` in generated quantities) and cmdstanr code to run it

The prior families now number 19, including skew-normal, logit-normal, Beta (mean, sample size), Weibull and scaled inverse-χ².

Priors can be saved to a **prior library** in any tab, loaded into any other tab (including the Model Lab and presets), and downloaded/uploaded as CSV.

The maths behind the Prior Lab lives in `R/prior_lab_*.R` (no Shiny code). The test script checks it against closed-form conjugate results, brute-force integration, exact grid posteriors, `lm`/`glm`/`MASS::glm.nb`/`MASS::polr`/`survival::survreg` fits, the `posterior` package's R-hat and ESS, and (when rstan is installed) compiles every generated Stan program:

```r
Rscript tests/test_prior_lab.R
```

## 🛠️ Technical Stack

  * **Language:** R
  * **Framework:** [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/)
  * **Bayesian Core:** functions adapted from [TeachBayes](https://bayesball.github.io/TeachBayes/) (`R/bayes_utils.R`) and the Prior Lab engine (`R/prior_lab_*.R`, base R only)
  * **Interface:** [bslib](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/) (Bootstrap 5 theme and page layout)
  * **Plotting:** [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) (via `TeachBayes`) & [plotly](https://plotly.com/r/)
  * **Data Manipulation:** [dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/) (implied by `magrittr` pipe `%>%`)
